title: New work orders for a flagged customer are billable while the setting is off
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer, flagged while the setting was on, with one asset, asset 1.
custom_steps:
1. Click New Work Order.
  2. Pick customer A.
  3. Pick asset 1.
  4. Save the new work order.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Work Order window opens.

Step 2:

  • No "Internal" badge and no info icon show next to customer A.

Step 3:

  • Asset 1 is picked.

Step 4:

  • The work order opens with no "Internal" badge.
  • It finishes with "Create invoice".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S1-R10: “Turning the toggle off hides the hint lines and the customer badges and leaves the flags on the customers. Open internal work orders are not touched: they keep their badge and close as internal. New work orders for a flagged customer are billable while the toggle is off. Turning it on again (with Save settings, like any other toggle) opens no modal: the customer badges and the hint lines come back and, on Save settings, for every flagged customer with open billable work orders, the dialog of S1-R11 is shown, one after another. New internal customers are flagged on Edit Customer (S1-R7).”
  • S2-N1: “If the setting is off, the New Work Order dialog shows no badge, hint or No Charge checkbox, and new work orders for flagged customers are billable. Open internal and no-charge work orders keep their classification, badge, orange header and category; they close as in Story 3 (S1-R10). Billable work orders offer no Convert to No Charge. While the setting is off, an open no-charge work order can still be converted to billable, and its category changed, from the menu; the Convert to Billable confirmation drops its second sentence. A customer change while the setting is off makes the work order billable whatever the new customer's flag; a No Charge mark survives a change to another regular customer.”
